surprises.head: Philadelphia kept finding open men against Karel Vejmelka
surprises.body: Vejmelka allowed 5 goals on 20 shots, worth 2.0 expected goals: 3.0 more than expected, though three of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 35 starts.

story.head: Drysdale has three assists as the Flyers beat the Mammoth
paras: Matvei Michkov got the scoring started for the Flyers midway through the first, but Dmitri Simashev made it 1-1 for Utah a minute and a half later. Travis Konecny restored the Flyers’ lead early in the second, in his first game back after missing ten games. Noah Cates made it 3-1 less than five minutes later. There were five goals in the third period alone. Christian Dvorak and Oliver Bonk scored four and a half minutes apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 5-1. Lawson Crouse and Simon Benoit fought midway through the period. Mikhail Sergachev and Logan Cooley scored just over a minute apart with four minutes left to cut Philadelphia’s lead to 5-3. Cole Knuble added an empty-net goal with a minute and a half left to make it 6-3. Jamie Drysdale finished with three assists.

The Mammoth had a little more of the play, but the Flyers made their chances count. Dan Vladař made 19 saves for the Flyers, and Karel Vejmelka allowed five goals on 20 shots. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Travis Sanheim, by our Swing measure. The Flyers improved to 4-8-4 and climbed off the bottom of the Metropolitan to seventh, while the Mammoth fell to 9-6-0, second in the Central.
